minutes.headline: ZBA granted Dance Paving a special permit for a contractor's yard at 691 Chase Road, with conditions.
minutes.summary: The Zoning Board of Appeals heard a continued special permit application from Dance Paving to run a contractor's yard on Chase Road. Board members questioned staffing, repairs, asphalt handling and the unpermitted driveway; one abutter raised water and well concerns. The board approved the permit with conditions on the trailer, asphalt and hazardous materials, then adjourned.

public_comment.topic: Asked about water runoff to adjoining properties, protection of his private well, the oil and water separator, whether the office trailer had been moved, and whether the site plan driveway matches the existing one.
A person who works for the company that took over the Elm Street, Fitchburg building said the applicant had been a close neighbor there; offered as context on being a good neighbor.

votes.motion: Approve the special permit for a contractor's yard at 691 Chase Road, with conditions: trailer removed six months after all approvals, no asphalt stored on site, no hazardous materials stored on site.

decisions.decision: Chair stated the special permit had been approved and read the post-decision notice (14-day filing with town clerk, 20-day appeal period, recording at registry, two-year lapse).
Wetlands and wastewater concerns left to the Planning Board and Conservation Commission; lighting must not spill onto abutters' property.
Board agreed to give temporary relief on the office trailer, tied to six months after the final permit.

what_happened.line: The Zoning Board of Appeals approved a special permit for Dance Paving to run a contractor's yard at 691 Chase Road, with conditions; the vote count was not audible.
Conditions: the office trailer must be removed six months after all approvals, and no asphalt or hazardous materials may be stored on site.
The board agreed to temporary relief on the office trailer, tied to six months after the final permit.
An abutter asked about runoff, protection of his private well and the oil and water separator; the board left wetlands and wastewater to the Planning Board and Conservation Commission.
The chair read the post-decision notice: filing with the town clerk, a 20-day appeal period, and a two-year lapse.

why_it_matters: A contractor's yard is now permitted on Chase Road, and neighbors with wells or runoff concerns must rely on the Planning Board and Conservation Commission, since the ZBA left those reviews to them.
